Studied: Deception.description:
🃏 You learned to lie well: improv theater, poker, a sales floor with quotas or a youth spent talking your way out of trouble.

🌱 You keep a story consistent, control your face and voice, and say true things that lead to false conclusions.
⚠️ Trained interrogators, people who know you, lie-detecting Quirks and paper evidence still catch you, and every lie needs upkeep.
⚖️ Fraud, false statements to police and impersonating a hero are crimes, and trust lost to a lie returns slowly.
🏫 It shows in an even voice, smooth answers and a memory for exactly what you told whom.

📈 Grants: Deception +15
Studied: Deception.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has practiced deception: keeping a story consistent, controlling face and voice, misdirecting attention and saying true things that lead to false conclusions. Prior study, not mastery: trained interrogators, people who know them well, lie-detecting Quirks and evidence on paper still catch them, and every lie needs upkeep. Not a license: fraud, false statements to police and impersonating a hero are crimes, and a lie found out costs trust that returns slowly. It shows in an even voice, smooth answers and a habit of remembering exactly what they told whom.
